Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden.
Hamza, drinking wine, cuts up the she-camels Ali would load with Idhkhir to pay for his wedding banquet, and retorts to the Prophet's rebuke, before drinking was prohibited.
When alcohol is prohibited, Anas spills Abu Talha's wine into Medina's streets, and a verse says believers who did good are not blamed for what they consumed before.
Ali's two she-camels, from his Badr booty and the Khumus, are mutilated by Hamza drinking with Ansari men; the Prophet rebukes him, but seeing him drunk, withdraws.
In Mecca in the Conquest year the Prophet declares that Allah and His Messenger have made the selling of wine unlawful.
Alcohol was banned when Medina's drinks were not from grapes; Anas spilled Abu Talha's date wine, Umar defined alcohol, and men killed at Uhud before the ban bore no blame.
Whoever drinks alcohol unrepentant is denied it hereafter; the Prophet chose milk over wine on his night journey; drinking portends the Hour, and a drinker is no believer while drinking.
Banned alcohol, mostly made from dates, was poured out; Umar said it comes from five things and clouds the mind; all intoxicants are unlawful, though some will deem them lawful.
Any intoxicating drink is unlawful whatever its name, while the Prophet liked sweets and honey; drinks of mixed dates counted as alcohol, and mixing fruits for a drink was forbidden.
Anas was serving his uncles a drink of ripe and unripe dates when alcohol was announced prohibited, and they told him to throw it away.
The Prophet had drinkers beaten with palm stalks, shoes, hands and garments, forbidding cursing them; Abu Bakr gave forty lashes, Umar forty then eighty; Ali said none were fixed.
When a man announced that all alcoholic drinks were prohibited, Abu Talha had Anas break the jars of date drink he was serving.
